questions.question: Additional comments:
How relevant did you find your traineeship for your future employment prospects? *
questions.answer: Depending on my future career. I worked a lot with mangrove forest and there does not appear to be a lot of the specific ecosystem in Denmark. However, I learned valued experiences in relation to data collection and knowledge provision from University of Nairobi. I would hope that future employers would see the value of my traineeship.

questions.question: How relevant did you find your traineeship for your academic programme at UCPH *
questions.answer: Extremely relevant. I have learned valuable skills and improved other ones. The traineeship complemented my studies but also expanded my academic profile in ways that would not have been possible on campus. The experiences I have learned by being in another country is unprecedented for my academic profile.

questions.question: Additional comments
How well did the academic level at UCPH coincide with the tasks completed during your traineeship? *
questions.answer: The academic level at UCPH coincided exceptionally well with the tasks I completed during my traineeship. My coursework in Forest and Nature Management provided a strong theoretical foundation in areas such as ecosystem dynamics, sustainable resource management, and socio-ecological systems all of which were applicable to my traineship which focused on mangrove forest in coastal Kenya.

questions.question: Please elaborate *
questions.answer:
For example, my understanding of forest ecology and community-based engagement and conservationfrom UCPH courses allowed me to design and conduct interviews with local stakeholders more effectively. The traineeship challenged me to apply my knowledge in real-world settings, where I had to adapt theoretical frameworks to address practical challenges, such as balancing conservation goals with local livelihoods. My experience reinforced my academic learning but made it clear to me the importance of interdisciplinary approaches in environmental management.

I think it was a perfect alignment between my studies and the traineeship which have strengthened my ability to bridge theory and practice essentially making my experience both academically enriching and professionally formative.

questions.answer: There was a lot of hiking groups where you could participate every weekend with different destinations. It was really nice to use it to mingle with local people and not just other international students. (AdventureGo, Nairobi)

questions.question: Which non-academic activities would you recommend to future trainees visiting the same destination (organization/city/region)? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking (AdventureGo, Nairobi). Music (Gekko Club, Nairobi). Tennis. Local parks.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting trainees see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Safari. Scuba diving. Hiking. Try going to a church cermony on a Sunday (quite different than other places).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your trainee host? *
questions.answer: Easy with some difficulties. Kenyan culture and Danish culture is almost polar opposites. But if you are open and willing to learn Kenyans are an open and warm people that will introduce your to their life and culture. Especially if you learn some Swahili phrases then you are considered a brother/sister.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of the destination (city/country)? *
questions.answer: Easy with some difficulties. Kenyan culture and Danish culture is almost polar opposites. But if you are open and willing to learn Kenyans are an open and warm people that will introduce your to their life and culture. Especially if you learn some Swahili phrases then you are considered a brother/sister.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer: Learn Swahili phrases/words. Being open for being approached because they are interested in knowing you and why you are here and where you come from. Especially if you are at the coastal regions.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to navigate in the religious aspect. Kenyans value religion highly whether it is islam, christianity or another religion they have great respect for a man of religion. As a man without any religious affilation it was some times a but difficult defending your "lack" of religion. So it would be easier to just say that you are some kind of religious even though you are not.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness. The tranquil and slow every day life. The idea of not to worry to much about things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer: Try go to a local bar to meet local people. Try the local food. Try safari - it is outstadingly beautiful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *
questions.answer: Get M-Pesa which make you able to pay everybody with your phone. (Need a Kenyan SIM-card).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a small village where you truly experienced the local life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the traineeship? *
questions.answer: Overcoming homesicknes and langauge barrierers.

questions.question: Is there anything UCPH could have done different (before/during/after) in regard to the traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: Better contact between host university and my.
